rationale: Evidence: iteration 8 (base_speed 1.0) scored 388.85, below the iteration 5 best of 417.25. The oval still finished 20 of 20 (completion time about 1.86 s), but s-bend progress fell from 0.56 to 0.35, and slalom progress stayed at 0.187 with exactly 1 line-loss event. Lowering speed therefore did not fix the slalom and cost s-bend progress. Iteration 7 showed the line-loss recovery mode (search_right) changes nothing. Speed is not the slalom limit, so the approved fallback applies: return base_speed to 1.2 and test kp alone. Change: controller.kp from 1.5 to 1.8, with all other fields at the iteration 5 baseline (base_speed 1.2, ki 0.5, kd 0.4, sensors at x = -0.05 to 0.05 and y = 0.07, sensor_size 0.012, line_loss last_direction). Expected result: more turn authority on the bend entry, so the slalom line loss may ease and slalom progress may rise above 0.2. The oval should still finish, since kd 0.4 provides damping. Risk: kp 1.8 with kd 0.4 may raise steering_oscillation above the current 0.21 to 0.30 range. Hypotheses: (a) turn authority, not speed, limits the slalom bend; (b) if slalom progress is unchanged, the slalom loss is set by sensor geometry at the sharpest entry, and the next test should be a sensor y or x change in a single step. Measurements wanted: per-track progress, finish rate, completion_time, line_loss_events, max_error and steering_oscillation, to see whether kp moves the slalom and whether the oval margin holds.
